candidate_relations.reason: Recurrent follicular lymphoma is the underlying cancer, not the psoriasiform eruption.
Pityriasis rubra pilaris is a differential for palmoplantar keratoderma but biopsy was a psoriasiform drug reaction.
Follicular lymphoma is the treated comorbidity, not the eruption.
Duvelisib-induced psoriasiform dermatitis is the same psoriasiform drug eruption with the PI3K-inhibitor culprit named.
Oxycodone-induced psoriasiform eruption asserts an incompatible primary culprit; PI3K inhibitors, not opioids, cause this pattern.
Drug-induced psoriasiform dermatitis is a wording variant of psoriasiform drug eruption.
Duvelisib-induced skin reaction names the likely drug but omits the psoriasiform morphology.
Duvelisib-induced psoriasiform eruption matches the reference morphology with compatible drug etiology.
Eczema is a different spongiotic pattern from this neutrophil-rich psoriasiform histology.
There is no allogeneic transplant to support graft-versus-host disease.
Seborrheic dermatitis does not explain plantar plate-like scale with drug-reaction histology.
TMP-SMX more often causes morbilliform/SJS reactions; attributing this psoriasiform eruption to it conflicts with the more plausible PI3K-inhibitor cause.
Oxycodone-induced pruritus is a symptom attribution, not psoriasiform drug eruption.
Drug-induced psoriasis is a commonly used alias for a psoriasiform drug eruption.
Psoriasis names the pattern but omits the required drug-induced etiology.
Drug-induced skin eruption omits the psoriasiform morphology.
Drug-induced psoriasiform eruption is the same diagnostic object as psoriasiform drug eruption.
Parakeratosis is a histologic finding, not the clinical diagnosis.
Duvelisib-induced rash is trigger-level and missing psoriasiform morphology.
Contact dermatitis is an exogenous spongiotic process, not this drug-psoriasiform histology.
